title: S27 — oracle masks on the six collapse families: how much of the 48-miss wall is mask-recoverable vs ink-destroyed
desc: S25 located the 95-bar wall: six families at ~0 (48/79 hard misses) fail at or before the mask. The decision the room now faces — better masks (classic, cheap) vs image-side recognition (ML, expensive) — needs the split between (a) mask fails but ink is intact, (b) ink itself destroyed. Method: for each collapse-family miss, regenerate the pre-degradation clean render with the same seed (generator is deterministic), take the TRUE ink mask from it, and run the unchanged reader downstream (deskew→segment→template match). If the letters read under the oracle mask, the miss is mask-recoverable; if they still fail, the degradation (or downstream stages on displaced/rotated pieces) owns it. Deliverable: per-family recoverability table + the lane decision it implies. Note: collage de-rotation (t-8717) and S7c wall masks already exist — this task measures the CEILING of that whole class of fixes, it does not build one. Parent: t-20261011-88dc.

history.note: S27 PR open @0ef1e46: oracle decomposition complete — mask-recoverable ceiling 19/48 (upper bound, clean-render oracle); collage+corrosion 0/16 with TRUTH masks (downstream dead: rotation defeats single-angle deskew, heavy-stroke pitted glyphs defeat templates); 0/29 case-only among still-misses. Verdict: mask-class fixes cap at +19 hard at most; 95-bar needs image-side recognition
